Subject: RFP: AI model governance questionnaire (initial send)

Jonas —

Thanks for taking our call earlier. Attached is the formal questionnaire NorthStar uses for potential vendors that operate or influence model-driven customer decisions (we call it the 'Model Risk & AI Governance Questionnaire'). We need detailed responses that map to the NIST AI RMF and a separate section for EU AI Act positioning (we operate in the US but have EU customers).

High-level asks:
- NIST alignment: where you map to Core functions (Govern, Map, Measure, Manage, Protect) and which practices you currently cover.
- EU AI Act: whether any of your hosted services would be classified as "high-risk" under the draft rules and how you mitigate if so.
- Eval/regression controls: methodology for evals, continuous monitoring, rollback/fallback policies, and how you detect quality regressions.

Can you confirm a target date for the completed questionnaire? Procurement would like answers and supporting artifacts (SOC2, pen test summary, model cards) by 3/24. Let me know any clarifying questions.

Best,
Elena
VP, Digital Risk & AI Governance
NorthStar Financial

Subject: Re: RFP: AI model governance questionnaire — technical annex (NIST / EU / eval)

Hi Elena, Jonas —

Following up with the technical detail you asked for. Summary below; I'll attach a short annex to the Drive with examples and anonymized regression artifacts.

1) NIST AI RMF mapping- Govern: We maintain documented policies for model onboarding, access controls, and third-party evaluations. Redwood provides customer-configurable data governance controls for Dedicated/Private.
- Map: We inventory training data provenance where available; for customer-provided fine-tuning sets we capture dataset manifests and hashing.
- Measure: Continuous evaluation pipelines process production traces against labeled holdout suites (safety, accuracy, bias) and compute drift/metric baselines.
- Manage: Model versioning, canary rollouts, and automated rollback triggers based on monitored quality SLOs.
- Protect: Encryption at rest/in transit, tokenization options, KMS integrations, and role-based access controls.

2) EU AI Act posture- Classification: Our hosted text-generation API can be used in use-cases that clients classify as "high-risk" (e.g., credit decisions). We do not classify the service itself as high-risk by default; instead we provide the controls expected for high-risk systems (documentation, post-market monitoring, incident reporting). For Dedicated/Private deployments we support customer-managed controls to meet the EU Act high-risk obligations.
- Mitigations: model cards, technical documentation, risk assessment templates, and traceability artifacts.

3) Eval and regression approach- Continuous eval: nightly and on-demand pipelines that run regression suites, adversarial tests, and safety checks.
- Regression detection: statistical tests (KS, KL divergence), performance delta thresholds, and behavioral test suites.
- Incident artifacts: for past regressions we keep anonymized trial inputs, model outputs, metric deltas, and post-mortem notes. We can provide 2 anonymized examples.
- Monitoring / alerts: integrated with PagerDuty and our Console; customers can configure SLO thresholds and automated fallback to pinned model versions.

4) Evidence & artifacts we can provide- SOC2 Type II (2025) certificate
- Summary of most recent penetration test (non-sensitive findings)
- Example model cards & version manifest
- Anonymized regression case studies and the alerting timeline

I'll upload a technical annex (PDF) and two anonymized regression examples to the shared Drive by EOD 3/19. If you want deeper raw datasets we can discuss an NDA and limited sharing.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Senior Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachment: pen-test-summary-2025.txt (brief findings list)
